name: Coral reef
notes: Tropical reef and reef flat: no true land plants except on the adjoining cay/strand (coconut, naupaka, morning glory); the reef itself is built of coral, encrusting coralline algae, Halimeda and turf/sea-grape algae, with seagrass on the back-reef lagoon floor. Drawn on the Great Barrier Reef, Caribbean and Red Sea; underwater species flagged.

canopy.name: Coconut palm
canopy.source: Cocos nucifera, reef cays and atoll islets throughout the tropics, 15-30 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Pisonia
canopy.source: Pisonia grandis, Indo-Pacific coral cays (Heron Island, Seychelles), soft-wooded seabird-forest tree 8-20 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Beach naupaka
shrub.source: Scaevola taccada, reef-cay strand throughout the Indo-Pacific, 1-3 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Octopus bush
shrub.source: Heliotropium (Tournefortia) foertherianum, Indo-Pacific coral cays and reef islands, silvery-leaved 1-6 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Beach morning glory
ground.source: Ipomoea pes-caprae, reef-cay sand strand, creeping vine 10-30 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Turtle grass
ground.source: underwater — Thalassia testudinum, Caribbean back-reef lagoons (T. hemprichii Indo-Pacific), broad-bladed seagrass 20-50 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Halimeda
ground.source: underwater — Halimeda opuntia, pantropical reef flats and slopes, calcified segmented green alga forming clumps 5-25 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Sea grapes alga
ground.source: underwater — Caulerpa racemosa, pantropical reef sand and rubble, runners with grape-like bladders 3-15 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Crustose coralline alga
ground.source: underwater — Porolithon onkodes, Indo-Pacific reef crest, pink encrusting coralline red alga that cements the reef, 1-3 cm crust — Wikipedia

ground.name: Turbinaria alga
ground.source: underwater — Turbinaria ornata, Indo-Pacific reef flats and crests, stiff brown alga with triangular blades 10-40 cm — Wikipedia
